claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys are primarily FCC soft ferromagnets with low coercivity.
Replacing Pd or Pt with W produces an equiatomic FeCoNiW alloy.
An equiatomic FeCoNiW composition contains approximately 25 at.% each of Fe, Co, Ni, and W.
Equiatomic FeCoNiW has a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
High-energy mixing followed by controlled annealing can produce a homogeneous FeCoNiW microstructure without significant phase segregation.
Introducing W into FeCoNi is expected to cause local lattice distortions or partial tetragonal distortion within an overall FCC matrix.
The W-induced structural distortions will serve as domain-wall pinning centers.
W has high atomic mass and strong spin-orbit coupling.
Substitutional W will increase local magnetocrystalline anisotropy in FeCoNiW.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase the coercive field.
Equiatomic FeCoNiW will have significantly greater coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
FeCoNiW will retain high saturation magnetization while its coercivity increases.
The coercivity enhancement is expected only near equiatomic composition and with a homogeneous microstructure.
Excessive phase separation or unwanted secondary phases may eliminate the coercivity enhancement.
A coercivity increase smaller than approximately 20% relative to FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary limits the hypothesis to homogeneous alloys without excessive phase separation, but the falsification rule treats observation of significant phase separation as falsifying the hypothesis. Phase separation could instead indicate failure to meet the stated applicability conditions rather than failure of the conditional mechanism.
